root_cause.text: In amdgpu_device_gpu_recover, the job's pasid is read after calling drm_sched_start(), which can asynchronously free the job via the TDR workqueue, leading to a use-after-free when accessing job->pasid.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The gpu recovery function calls drm_sched_stop() and later drm_sched_start(). drm_sched_start() restarts the tdr queue which will eventually free the job. If the tdr queue frees the job before time out callback completes, the job will be freed and we'll get a UAF when accessing the pasid." The patch caches pasid early with `int pasid = job ? job->pasid : -EINVAL;` and later uses the cached value instead of dereferencing job->pasid.

candidates.rationale: Controls entry into the code block where the use-after-free occurs; without this condition the vulnerable statements are not reached.
Declaration of ti, which is later assigned from the vulnerable pasid access; though not directly vulnerable, it is part of the data flow.
Dereferences the job pointer (reads it) to check for NULL; if the job has been freed asynchronously, this read itself is a use-after-free.
Directly reads job->pasid after the job may have been freed by drm_sched_start; this is the primary use-after-free access.
Uses ti which was obtained from the vulnerable pasid read; if the pasid was corrupted due to UAF, this call may operate on invalid data.
Continuation of the previous line; dereferences ti->task under the assumption ti is valid, but ti may be invalid due to the UAF in the previous line.

vuln_statements.explanation: Directly reads job->pasid after drm_sched_start() may have asynchronously freed the job, causing use-after-free.
Dereferences the job pointer to check for NULL; if job was freed asynchronously, this read is itself a use-after-free.
Uses the ti pointer that may have been corrupted due to the use-after-free on job->pasid, leading to invalid data access.
Dereferences ti->task if ti is non-NULL; ti may be invalid (from corrupted pasid or freed memory) due to the use-after-free.
Controls entry to the code block where the use-after-free occurs; without this condition the vulnerable accesses would not be reached.
